name: agent-builder-optional-release-agent
body:
The distributed `agent-builder` agent template `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (product source embedded into the `apg` binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`) must be able to scaffold an OPTIONAL, per-repo `release-agent` — the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. Unlike the distributed suite agents, the `release-agent` is GENERATED per repo, never distributed: it needs repo-specific release-artefact write grants (version files, formulae, changelog, …) and the repo's remote/branch conventions, interviewed per repo exactly like the build gates.

Its shape: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`; no `question` (it routes questions through the coordinator); it never actions Feedback — it returns an ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim like every generated agent. It is grant-unusual in exactly one way: `git push *` and `git tag *` are `allow` (autonomous once invoked), where every OTHER generated agent keeps them `ask` (human-approved).

The `release-agent` performs the repo's release: it is granted the release-adjacent git ops (tagging and pushing the branch and tags) plus write access to the repo's project-specific release artefacts. The `codebase-navigator` dispatches it through the `task` tool ONLY after obtaining **explicit user consent** — the human gate is that consent, captured before dispatch, not a per-command prompt.

This is a deliberate CARVE-OUT of the repo's recurring "push/tag remain human acts" rule (the scoped law is `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`): the rule continues to bind every other agent and path; only the deliberately-invoked release-agent is exempt, and only behind the consent gate.

The carve-out is an AGENT-policy statement, NOT a binary one. The `apg` binary still never pushes or tags: its git2 `default-features = false` rationale (`Cargo.toml`, `src/git/mod.rs`) and its "the git CLI is never shelled out to" statements (`src/git/**`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs`) remain TRUE and are NOT changed; the e2e tests asserting the binary's git2-only behaviour (`tests/git_e2e.rs`, `tests/project_cmd_e2e.rs`) are NOT touched. `scripts/release.sh` itself still never pushes — the release-agent may run it and then push/tag itself.

Surfaces to edit (all real `docs` File nodes in the branch graph):
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` — add the optional `release-agent` to the generated set (the roster intro, a `### release-agent (optional)` section, the workflow interview bullet, and the step-4/step-5 scaffold) and its grant shape (push/tag `allow`, repo-specific release-artefact edits, interviewed); scope its own "push/tag remain human-approved" prose (currently ~lines 90, 172-173, 289, 314-320, 376-378) to state the carve-out.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` — state that the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE tasking the release-agent; add `release-agent` to its `task` allowlist (currently lines 6-15); scope its "push/tag remain human acts" clause (currently lines 460-461).
- `AGENTS.md` — document the optional release-agent and the consent gate, and scope the "push/tag remain human acts" statements (currently lines 107-108, 130-131, 546-548, 559, 795).

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` offers and scaffolds the optional per-repo `release-agent`: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`, no `question`, returning ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claims; its push/tag grant is `allow` while every other generated agent's push/tag stays `ask`; its release-artefact write grants are interviewed per repo.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` states the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching the release-agent, and its `task` allowlist contains `release-agent`.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the release-agent, the consent gate, and the scoped push/tag rule.
- The binary-side "never shells out to the git CLI" statements and `scripts/release.sh`'s "never pushes" behaviour are unchanged; `Cargo.toml`, `src/git/**`, `src/project_cmd/mod.rs` and the e2e tests asserting the binary's git2-only behaviour are NOT edited.
- Scope is product source + the repo guide only: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are NOT edited. No binary change, no test change.
